The Storm abateing on the 30 off July I Surveyed our watter and provisions and found them in good Condission: 2 Months of all Sorts, according to Computation, and theirupon Consulted with all my officers what was best to be done. Wee concluded that in the Courses Steered they designed to go to the Northward off the Islands off Fairo , So in hopes that wee might meett with them their, I spent 9 days, butt Finding all in vain, I Resolved to make the best off our way For the First port that I cold get in Saffty to in England or Scotland. But
when I came near the Ferth the wind blew very hard So that I cold not cary my topsails with less then both Reeffes in, the wind at W. b So. to With. So I Resolved to make the best of my way For Newcastle.

Butt on the 14 off August in the morning see 2 Ships ahead off me. So I tacked and Stood to the Northward. They gave me Chase all that day, and although wee careyed away our maintopmast, wee bore away and Steered Such courses as wee Lost them.

On the 15th in the morning, having got up another topmast, butt the Riging not Set Fast, when I see that a priviteer that had given us Chase 2 hours, I see would inffallably Speak with us. I Resolved, as God is my witness, to deffend my Charge with the Last Drop off my blood, and so caled all my people together and prepared our Selves to Receive him. He came under our Lee quarter, in order, as I believe, to board us, butt Finding too warm a Receipt, hee Shared off and Lay under our Lee bow, and their plied us with a very warm Fire, most From Small arms. For, I believe, an hour and a halff beffore I Received that wound that disabled me. And then, by the help of Mr. Dupuy, I was Corryed down and ordered the Rest to go to Close quarters, which was perfformed and prepared For with the best provision I cold make, having 6 powder Chests upon the quarter deck and 16 quarter Shells, and upon the Forecasle 2 powder Chests, and my Small arms in the best Condission I cold Keep them.

Indead, the behaviour off my mate Griffin I cannot Commend,
For beffore I was wounded in the Knee, hee had Lefft his quarters above a quarter off an hour, and taken with him all who was Givein him to take care off, telling them, as I understand since, that I had ordered them to Close quarters. And when Thomas Studes would have come up, hearing me and the rest upon the deck busy in Entertaining and Returning the Enemies Fire, hee would not Let him, and when the Priviteer putt off, in spite of all that I cold do to persuade him to go up and incorage the people, he Refused, telling me that it was Impossible to Stand upon the quarter deck.

So Mr. Dupuy Looking down, as I Remember, I beged off him to help me up , and Mr. Griffin helped him to get me up, butt Sit and Served outt the powder him Selff Some time affter, till the Enemy was quite outt off muscat Shot and making the best off his way. So having sit till I was cold, my wounds become very painffull, and then they carried me down and putt me to bed, and I ordered Mr. Griffin to make the best of their way For Noraway, the wind being Westerly, with which there was no hopes of gaining the coast off England or Scotland.

Butt the Management that was used affter I was down, I pray God Let never any honest man be a specktater off. For as I was infformed by the Carpenter Next morning, hee went to his Cabin and did not so much as inform them what course to Steer. And Sum time affter hee was going S.Et., when his Course was Et. And when I asked him what hee mooned by that Course, hee went to his drafft and told me hee would bear away, For hee had not minded beffore the wind then being at S.S.With. And when She came beffore the wind, She Shiped Sum watter. And presently I heard such distraction and Swaring that wee Should all be drowned, as if the Ship had been going to the bottom.

I asked the matter, and hee told me She shiped watter over the gunell, att which I ordered him to go N. b W. with the
wind upon that quarter till hee came in the Latitude off 57 30' N. and then to go away E.N.Et. In all this Time I beged off him to get up the maintop Saill, but cold not persuade him to do it.

The day beffore wee ware taken he told me hee was in the Latitude I had ordered. So I ordered him to Steer away E.N.Et., and att 8 o'clock Caled him and told him that I did not think it sofa For him to Stand till 12, and that I would have him bring to att 10. Butt being so drunk that I could Scarce get him to Speak, hee told me one watch cold not doe it, and So, Contrary to my order, Fell asleep, as I was infformed, and stood till 12.

In the breek off Day they told me that wee where within 2 miles off the Shore off Uteland , to my great Mortyffication, yet praiseing God that so many Soulls had Escaped So Eminent a danger. Some time affter they told me they See 3 Saill off hagboatts, which in hope to have got a pilett outt off them, I ordered them to endeavour to Speak with them. Butt they whithered us and would not bear down. So being, by the Manidgment as I had seen, without a better pilett, the Next Night would produce a grave For all off us, I ordered him to Spread the Ensign in the maintop mast shrouds to See if any off them would bear down to us. But they would not.

Then hee cam and told me that they see 2 Ships to Leeward off us. I asked him what them Looked Like. Hee told me hee believed them to be 2 off the Dutch Fleatt, and asked me if hee should bear down to them. And I told him to do what hee would, and thinking that if they ware an Enemy and to Leeward, they would unavoidably Speak with us, wee having No main top Saill. So God Almighty knows and be my Record whether my Liffe or the Ship I had in my Charge was most dear to me. For while I am on this side the grave, the Lose off her hath taken away that which may be Imputed the Enjoyment off the Liffe in me.

And as For Those dimentts , I only desire you to consider whether if I had had them all and Free off a bad consequence, whether they would have Surmounted my Intrests in the Ship or no, whereas I took but one off the three parcels into my Custody, the prime cost off which, according to the bill off Laideing, is about 600 pagodus; and whether that cold make me satisffaction or not, I Lieve you to be Judge off what Interest I had in the Ships Saffty by what is hear Inserted.
When you pleass to order me to wait upon you and the party their, which did not appear yesterday, I shall be Ready. Your humble Servant, Jose: Tolson.
To Capt. Bowry and the Rest off the owners off Mary Gally .

note.value: PAPER 79. (GRIST'S CHARGE OF COWARDICE AGAINST TOLSON AND GRIFFIN.)

text.p: March 15th 1707/8.

Captn. Bowrey, Sir, The Bearer hereof desired me to Inform you he was not indebted any matter in the Ship's Book, to which I can swear too. His Circumstances being very poor and mean, I suppose You will not deny paying him part of his Wages, considering he was a Person that behaved himself very bravely in the Engagement with the French Privateer, when Mr. Tolson and his Rascally Mate Griffin left the Deck, and consequently, in their belief, Gave up the Ship Mary Gally , the former having a wound in his Excuse, the latter not only keeping between Decks in the time of Engaging, but hindering those that were Quartered with
him from coming up to assist those that kept the Deck, as your Kinsman Thomas Studds and others that were with him informed me after the Engagement was over. I am Sir, Your humble Servant, Alias Grist.
Attested to per ... John Eliot.
To Captn. Thomas Bowrey, Present.

note.value: PAPER 94. (GRIST'S STATEMENTS AS TO HIS DEBT TO TOLSON.)

text.p: May the 19th 1708.

Captain Bowrey, Sir, I am informed Captain Tolson avouches to you and the other Owners that the 190 Rex Dollars paid Mr. Moor for my accountt was not to run upon the Bottom of the Ship and the premium, or advance upon it, but to be left to the Discretion of the Owners att the safe arrival of the Ship.

I wonder he should affirm so known an Untruth, when in Mr. Griffins Hearing and also in Mr. Dupuys, more then once or twice, this was the verbal agreement, that in case of the Loss of the Ship, that Debt to be null and void. And when we first discoursed concerning that Debt, Griffin was by, and offered to pay Mr. Moor the money for my account, in case the Captain was not free to pay it. Also was paid out of the Ships stock near double the Sum for the account of Mr. Dupuy, on the very same Terms. And consequently the Owners may, with the same Equity, make a Demand of the money from Mr. Dupuy, as stop any part of my Wages or Ships Debts upon that account.

And again, Sir, att the juncture when this money was paid, how inconsistent must it be with your Interest, nay with common Reason, to lessen the Ships Stock upon any other Terms then
the Bottom of the Ship, especially considering the smallness of it, and that there was no necessity for it, because I could be supplied by another Hand. And if the money was Lent upon any other Terms (as it was not), then the premium would have made but a small amount to the Debt.

When I saw Captain Tolson last, I showed him the Terms wee agreed on in Refference to that money. All his answer was, he could not remember it. But I find he can remember and forget as suits best his Convenience.

And, Sir, as to that Objection about paying my part of wages Due to the Ships Company, that does concern me Solely. Some of them are more indebted to me then my Share amounts too, and if any of them, for favours shown them in the voyage and out of Consideration to my present Circumstances, should be easy as to that matter, none of the Owners will suffer on that Account.
Therefore, I crave the favour of you, Sir, to Get in my money as soon as possible.

As to that matter concerning the 592 Rex Dollars said to be twice Charged in Mr. Moors Account Current, all I can say to the matter is that I wrote after a Copy, and as Captain Tolson Dictated, the account was delivered to him, and he only Received the Balance. And if Mr. Moors paid that Sum less then his Due, it is my Belief it was not with Desine, because that after he took his Account from me, in order to know the Balance Due from him, he came the next morning and said he was not satisfied with that account, because Captain Tolson had not Gave him Creditt for One half of some Charge he was att in Getting his Goods ashore, it being, as he affirmed, agreed so between them, and brought an Account that he made up, affirming the Balance came Short of the Captains Demand.

Now the Querie lays, if he was sensible of his Advantage, why would he not rather be Quiet and set down the Gainer, rather then occasion the overlooking the Account again, which must have found out the mistake, unless it must be allowed him to be a very honest Gentleman, as most that ever dealt with him avouch. But as to Captain Tolson's Character of him, I don't wonder att it, for I never Knew him speak well of any man, besides Captain Jones.

And as to that other business, concerning the Sharing the 500 Dollars that Mr. Moor allowed for Demorage, if I was to appear before the Tribunal of God to morrow, I could with Safety Swear
the minute before that (to the best of my memory) on Monday Evening, Captain Tolson, Mr. Griffin and my Self being att Mr. Vanderbegs att Batavia, he spoke to us to come with him into his Chamber, and having Shut to the Door, made to us the following proposition, Vizt. , that in order for sharing the 500 Dollars, he would first take out 1/6 part, as being 1/6 part Owner; that I should have 1/24 part out for the same reason, and then the remainder should be divided in fifths, he taking two fifths, and the remaining 3/5 to be equally divided between Mr. Griffin and me.
Tic well for him Dupuy is absent and Griffin and I at variance. Otherways this part of the world would be too Hot to hold him.

I am informed, Sir, that my Name is signed to several of Captain Tolsons papers. I am sensible that to some that Mr. Griffin and Mr. Dupuy signed too, I signed also, but I am fully assured to none of any vast importance in the latter part of the voyage.
I beg pardon, Sir, for being so tedious, and am, Sir, Your Humble Servant, E. Grist
To Capt: Tho: Bowrey, In Marine Square, near Rattcliff Highway: Present.

note.value: PAPER 98. (GRIST'S REQUEST TO BOWREY TO RECOVER HIS CLAIMS FOR HIM.)

text.p: August 9th 1708

Sir, I received your Note, but withal desire you to consider the Debts due from the Ships Company to me. As your Business could not be well performed by several on board the Ship without my assisting them with Clothes, &c. (which was by the Captains Order), it is very hard if I must have no allowance for so necessary supply.

Your answer heretofore was, I must have my Recourse to Captain Tolson, who Gave me Order for Serving the men; but if he be put past a possibility of paying me, I know not to whom to apply besides your Self and the rest of the Owners.

What I have all ready Given Oath too, I am, and ever shall be, ready to attest too, though upon my Death Bed. But there can be no policy in Serving you farther to my Cost, which will follow if Captain Tolson recover no part of his wages. I desire, Sir, that Equity May have its Course. Then, I am well asshur'd, I shall be Considered.

I was chiefly accessory to saving the Ship once (which without vanity I may avouch), but never lent a helping hand to the loss of her. I am, Sir, Your humble Servant, Alias Grist To Captain Thomas Bowrey, att his House in Marine Square, near Rattcliff Highway; Present.
June the 15th 1708.

Sir, The Severty off your persecution is such that I cannot Apprehend your Intention to bee Less then that you Intend to drive me off the Stage, off which my Sad circomstances off the Loss off my Limes and all that I had in the world makes me weary off; and you cannot be more desirous off it then I am Free to make you a Sacriffice off it.

The great God be Judge off the Reason I have given you (For I know none) to proceed against me in this Nature. Your deserning eye is able to pentrate into the unjustness off those False accusations which the devil and malis hath Invented against me, off which God alone can be Judge, Since I Find nothing will Stick with them to make their False Stories plausible, So that if they can butt invent, they can affirm. So that I can not pretend
to compose any matters till I know what they are, and as you told me that their Memory might not bee good att a time when they might make their affidavit, So that I Find if they have not Invented enough, they Intend to do it.

I only desire you to Consider the Case and do by me as you would doe by your Selff, and you would Never incorage Such insolent villines, which plainly doth appear that none in my Circomstance was Capable off keeping under Government without some Roger, For which their malis hath Invented those Stories, Finding you Ready to Incorage and give Ear to their ungrateffull and False using me.

My not deserning your perffections early hath proved my utter Ruin, For I always did Suppose Captain Bowryes virtues to have been Equally composed with those pirffections off wisdom I Deserned in him, butt to my greatt disatisffaction, I Find these perffections may be Saperatte, and honour goes no Forther then Interest can cary it. So that my want of Fore Knowledge hath made my Liffe a pray to a merciless Enemy, to whom, God is my Record, I have given no Just ocation, Neither Do I know when ? what you can Expectt butt my Liffe, Except you would have me be your Slave, which I would willingly bee, if you could turn my Skin From White to black, if that would apeass you. But you cannot Expectt that I can make any Such Sacryffice with my Known Vizogminy ; and according to what I can Fore See, you can have no other End then one off those, my misffortins having made my Condition Reather to be pitied than Envied, being Reduced to become a pensioner to the Charty off those which is pleased to admit me to their table and to assist me in the time off my Conffinement, to whom I am engaged even for the meett I eatt and the Cloths I ware, Even For more then I can tell which way to repay or am worth in the World.

So that my condition being Such, I hope to Let you have your Ends Shortly, butt not till I can Leave that behind me that shall make appear your Crewltty. And although I never intend to survive the discovery off any Secrets Committed to me, I shall not Faill to Leave that behind me that shall.

If you please to answer these, I desire you to send it to the Jameco Coffy house or To the Union Coffy house, For the
difference that is betwixt us is a Secret to my wife, and I desire you would not disclose it. Yours, Jose: Tolson To Captain Bowry, Living in Mereen Square, Merchant, London.

note.value: PAPER 101. (TOLSON TO BOWREY REGARDING A PETTY CLAIM FOR BOARD FOR A PASSENGER ON THE HOMEWARD VOYAGE.)

text.p: July the 6. 1708.
Sir, I send you these, desiring your Answer, that I may make Demands as Easy and Reasonable and short as I can.

As concerning the note to Mr. Finch att the Cape , I desire you to take a right consideration off the matter, wherein you See that he even made you criditure For a passenger att my own table, which you know I can with Justice demand, and I cannot see any Reason it can be Reffused, and Likewise Several others off the men that Received money off me att the Cape , which will, I do not Question, be allowed me. But it will contain a Long and tedious Consideration to an arbitrator. So that if you are willing to pay that note to Mr. Finch, I am willing to Let all such tedious demands pas by. And as I have made you creditor For all, I cannot Forbore complaining when you Reffuse so small a matter.
So I desire you will Let me know your Resoltt in the matter in a Line to me directed to Mr. Johnsons. Your Servant, Jose. Tolson
To Captain Bowry, Living in Maroon Square, London

note.value: PAPER 103. (TOLSON TO BOWREY ON THE CASE OF WRIGHT VS. ELLIOTT, AND SUGGESTING ARBITRATION AS TO THE OTHER MATTERS BETWEEN THEM.)

text.p: Sir, I understand by Mr. Hamon that you have Reported that I was flouted outt off the court in the Late Trial betwixt Mr. Wright and John Eliot. And as I doe believe you are Imposed upon by mallishous persons Infformation, I hope, as it is a thing that has to bee proved, that you will doe me the Justice as to make a due Inquirey into the matter and give a just Report thereof to those whom you have, in my opinion, undiscreetly made bold to Scandlies me with.

In this I hope you will not Faill, since it is a thing that Honour and Justice binds every body to that is misled by False infformation. As For several other Lies that you have been infformed in, I blame the authors and not you. Butt, this being a thing that is very easy to be proved, I think you doe me unjustice if you doe not make me Reparation in it.

I cannot even my selff with saffty to come and speak with you, understanding that their is an action out against me by Capt. Bapty For his 2 servants wages, and I am unwilling to lie in a prison and doth not Know where to get baill. So I desire that you will speak to him and see what may be done in the matter without Rigour.

For the other matters in queston, I am willing to Reffare it to 2 Comanders off ships, you chuseing one and I another, if you will give me your promise that att our meeting you will not endeavour me being arrested. Butt things may, with the best off our Indivers, be accommodated For the beneffitt off my Selffe, you, and the rest of the owners, which will perhaps not Fall out so,
if Rigorous meenes be used and things put out off the Channel they aught to run in.

So I desire you will come with my brother-IN-LAW Johnson to me, that wee may consult who to leive the matter to; and if you are not inclined to leive it to arbitration, that wee may consult other meens to bring it to a speedy trial, which will be the Costliest way off arbitration, and I believe not to our advantage.
I do not abscond For any thing that you have to say against me, but will appear att your somence att any time. Your servant, Jose: Tolson
P.S. Mr. Johnson will waitt on you att change time and I shall not be Fore off.
To Capt. Bowry.
